content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP® Certification in Arlington

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your PMP® Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review the specific hour and year thresholds for your background—a bachelor's degree paired with three years of experience, or a high school diploma with five years. Gather transcripts and project records now to streamline your application later.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP® Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Our instructor-led format spans multiple sessions across weeks or an intensive schedule—you choose the pace that fits your work calendar. All instruction occurs online; attend from anywhere, including your Arlington office or home.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application & Fee
steps_items.text: After finishing your 35 contact hours, create your PMI account and complete the formal PMP® application. Document your project experience, education, and training completion through PMI's portal. Submit your fee and await PMI's review—typically completed within days—before you can schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the PMP® Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor Q&A sessions—to reinforce bootcamp content. Schedule your computerized exam through Pearson Vue at a testing center near Arlington or via remote proctoring. The exam tests your readiness to lead projects in Defense, Government, Aerospace, Technology, and other industries.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP® certification lasts three years. Earn continuing education units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, or completing self-study activities in project management. Renew before expiration by submitting your PDUs and a small fee to PMI. Staying current keeps your credential valuable as your career advances.
